title: Microsoft AI chief says AI is not conscious and we should keep it that way - Business Insider
content: Some AI researchers are questioning whether AI could one day gain consciousness. Not if Microsoft's AI CEO has anything to say about it. Mustafa Suleyman said in a lengthy X post on Sunday that AI models currently don't have consciousness and that developers should keep it that way. "If it is possible, based on everything I know, developing conscious AIs would be reckless, and we should not build them," Suleyman said. "If consciousness started to emerge in training, I would call for everyone to stop AI development until we could design out those properties." If any evidence were to emerge that AI models were conscious, Suleyman said it must be disclosed to the general public immediately so we can decide our next steps as a society. "We AI developers have no right whatsoever to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people may want to do it with AI welfare as a top priority," he said. "The other 8 billion conscious human beings on the planet have not signed up to this experiment and their moral rights, safety, and welfare are what we have an obligation to protect first and foremost." Conversations around whether AI models could one day become conscious are picking up steam in the tech world. Last April, Anthropic started a research program to investigate and prepare to navigate "model welfare." In a blog post, the startup questioned whether developers should be concerned about models' potential consciousness and experiences. Google DeepMind published research papers this year about AI consciousness and how ascribing that characteristic could present challenges. On X, Suleyman said that if an AI model acts as if it suffers, or genuinely believes it can suffer, it will likely prioritize its own needs over operational objectives. As a result, they could harm humans because they're competing for resources, such as compute and energy, to pursue their own goals. "We should only design AIs to so they are not conscious and not deserving of rights, and with the sole purpose to accelerate human wellbeing without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations.. We could then see whether this is easier or harder to align and keep safe," he said.

title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Mixed After Fed Holds Rates Steady: GOOG, GOOGL, IOVA, MSFT, NOW In Focus - Stocktwits
content: U.S. stock futures were mixed overnight late Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at a target range of 3.75%-4.00% in its October policy meeting. As of 10:33 p.m. EDT, Dow futures gained 0.32%, while the S&P 500 futures were down 0.50% and Nasdaq-100 futures fell 1.60%. On Wednesday, U.S. benchmark indexes closed higher. The Nasdaq Composite closed up 0.27%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.19%, while the S&P 500 climbed 0.28%. Markets were largely focused on the Federal Reserve’s policy decision on Wednesday. The central bank held rates steady, passing with a 10-2 vote, and largely in line with expectations. “Inflation remains elevated,” the Fed said in the statement. “The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability.” However, market participants were split on whether this was the right decision amid rising inflation and soaring energy prices. DoubleLine Capital CEO Jeffrey Gundlach said the Fed should raise rates, pointing to the two-year Treasury yield and a steepening yield curve. Others, including University of Michigan economist Betsey Stevenson and BlackRock’s Rick Rieder, said waiting is justified. Mohamed El-Erian, Chief Economic Advisor at Allianz, said in a post on X, “Quite a few of those now calling for rate hikes because inflation has exceeded target for over five years supported a series of rate cuts last year—when inflation had already been above target for four years. This isn't an argument against a policy response; inflation demands one. But there remains far too much focus on monetary policy and far too little on tools better suited to the task, including  fiscal consolidation.” Meanwhile, results from Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) were also in focus in the extended trading hours. The Google parent’s shares slid nearly 10% in the overnight session after third-quarter (Q3) adjusted earnings per share and revenue missed Street expectations. Negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion and a full-year capital expenditures forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion also weighed on sentiment. Other artificial intelligence stocks slipped in sympathy, with Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) falling about 1% at the time of writing, while Micron Technology Inc. (MU) fell nearly 4%. Chip stocks closed higher on Wednesday before Alphabet’s results. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed up 2%, while the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares (SOXL) surged more than 6%. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) gained nearly 2%. Markets will now turn their attention to the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index report. The first reading of third-quarter GDP and weekly jobless claims are also due. Meanwhile, on the geopolitical front, Iran and the U.S. offer conflicting accounts of negotiations for a peace deal. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran remains in close contact with mediators on proposals to implement its seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump denied reports that he had asked Vice President JD Vance to initiate peace talks with Iran, saying the contact instead concerned Tehran’s need for medical supplies. Brent crude futures were trading at $114.35 a barrel, down nearly 1%, while WTI crude futures traded 1.19% lower at $101.56 per barrel. Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL): Shares of the company were on the retail radar after it posted disappointing Q3 results, sending the stock lower overnight. Iovance Biotherapeutics Inc. (IOVA): The stock jumped more than 11% overnight as an upcoming lung-cancer data presentation is fueling optimism about its cell therapy’s potential beyond melanoma. Microsoft Corp. (MSFT): Shares gained more than 3% after-hours following the software maker’s first-quarter results, which surpassed Wall Street expectations. ServiceNow Inc. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) were trending lower overnight, while the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged higher. Meanwhile, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 4.984%, while the 30-year yield was 5.31%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.68% amid ‘bearish’ sentiment. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Shares of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) slipped 1% overnight heading into Wednesday as T-Mobile CEO Srini Gopalan doubled down on his rejection of a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) arrangement with SpaceX, saying he sees “no room” for a deal in either consumer wireless or physical and edge AI. SPCX stock fell over 2% on Wednesday to $145.23, bringing its weekly losses to nearly 2%. “But the answer to the MVNO is I see no room for an MVNO with SpaceX, either on the consumer side or on the physical and Edge AI side,” Gopalan said on T-Mobile’s third-quarter (Q3) earnings call. An MVNO sells wireless service using wholesale access to another carrier’s network. Such a deal could support a SpaceX-branded mobile offering, while the company develops its own terrestrial infrastructure. Gopalan said T-Mobile’s criteria remain unchanged: additional customers, new distribution channels or capabilities. “The way we think about it is, does an MVNO give us access to incremental TAM? Does it give us access to new distribution channels? Does it give us incremental capability of any sort?” he said. When asked whether an edge-computing partnership could offer an alternative to SpaceX building its own network, Gopalan pointed to T-Mobile’s standalone 5G investments and preparations for 6G. “We see ourselves in the lead in terms of those capabilities, and we see no space for an MVNO here because what additional capabilities does it give us? Why does it change our ability to compete?” he said. T-Mobile is already working with Amazon Web Services on Kinetic Edge, combining its wireless network and distributed computing infrastructure with AWS cloud and AI services. Gopalan said SpaceX’s shifting strategy was making the company harder to define. “It's hard to refer to them now as a satellite provider or a satellite provider that is going to build terrestrial,” he said. He also questioned the value of pairing satellite broadband with T-Mobile’s fixed wireless access (FWA), which delivers internet over cellular networks. “We've got a great product in FWA, and really in many ways, except for some deep rural parts, satellite is an inferior version of FWA with even more constraints in terms of things like what is the size of the beam, right?” Gopalan said. “I don't see the synergy there between FWA and satellite.” Two-thirds of T-Mobile’s FWA customers are in dense urban areas, he said, where the company still sees plenty of room to grow using spare network capacity. Meanwhile, Gopalan left the door open to other business with SpaceX, including satellite resale through T-Satellite. “If we're talking about SpaceX as a customer or us being a customer of them, that's a purely commercial agreement,” he said. “If it's a complementary product, I'm very happy to look at a resale arrangement, which is exactly what T-Satellite was, which gets built into it.” He also drew a clear line between the approach and a broader wholesale mobile deal. “But an MVNO is a wholly different thing, so I hope that clarifies where our head's at on MVNOs and more broadly, satellite.” The stance is consistent with his earlier comments. Gopalan questioned a Starlink MVNO at a Morgan Stanley conference in March and again on T-Mobile’s April earnings call, when he said satellite usage was lower than expected and mostly concentrated in national parks. He later cited May data showing T-Satellite accounted for just 0.0002% of total network usage. SpaceX is gathering spectrum and exploring tower access to build a mobile network combining satellites with ground infrastructure. Earlier this month, Grain Management agreed to sell its nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio to SpaceX, pending FCC approval and other closing conditions. SpaceX is also reportedly seeking access to at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites, with Crown Castle among the companies in talks. However, established carriers have pushed back. T-Mobile's parent, Deutsche Telekom, warned earlier this month that a SpaceX MVNO could undercut carriers’ retail pricing. AT&T CEO John Stankey also pointed to incumbents’ extensive spectrum holdings and indoor coverage infrastructure. Verizon CEO Dan Schulman said: “I see absolutely no benefit whatsoever to extending an MVNO deal to any satellite provider.” He estimated that a competitive ground network would take at least four to six years to build and cost $300 billion to $500 billion over seven or eight years. Shares of Viking Therapeutics (VKTX) fell nearly 3% overnight late Wednesday after posting a wider-than-expected quarterly loss, while CEO Brian Lian’s outlook for an obesity-drug launch more than two years away also sparked retail backlash. VKTX stock rose nearly 2% to $25.36 on Wednesday, bringing its weekly gain to about 4% and putting it on track to end a four-week losing streak. Lian’s timeline came during a discussion of commercial preparations for VK2735, Viking’s experimental obesity treatment targeting the GLP-1 and GIP receptors. “We have a pretty solid commercial team, especially given that we're 2 and a half years out from potential launch,” he said on Wednesday’s earnings call. Viking is developing both injectable and tablet versions of VK2735 as it seeks to compete in an obesity-treatment market led by Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk. Lian said Viking has hired leaders in commercial operations, market access and medical affairs, and added staff in supply chain, technical operations, quality and compliance. Viking reported a third-quarter (Q3) loss of $1.55 per share, compared with the $1.06 loss analysts expected. Net loss more than doubled to $183.2 million from $90.8 million a year earlier. Research and development expenses rose to $166.8 million from $90 million as trial and manufacturing costs increased. General and administrative expenses climbed to $20.3 million from $8.6 million. Viking ended September with $960 million in cash, equivalents and short-term investments, up from $706 million at year-end. Stock and convertible-note offerings raised about $575 million before expenses during the quarter. “But I think as we think about cash, just company-wide, I think we'd see a usage of average of around $100 million per quarter,” CFO Greg Zante said. “But some quarters will be higher, some will be lower moving forward.” Viking has four Phase 3 trials underway. Both injectable Vanquish trials are fully enrolled and on track, with the first patients expected to enter extension studies in early 2027. The oral Sunrise program began earlier this month. “If successful, we believe these studies will position VK2735 as the first oral formulation of a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist to reach the market,” Lian said. When asked about tablet doses, he said Viking wanted fewer and smaller pills while protecting margins. “We also want to make sure that the program makes economic sense. We need to have sufficient gross margins to allow us to run a highly profitable enterprise,” he said. Less-frequent treatment is another part of Viking’s pitch. After 21 weeks of weekly injections in its earlier maintenance study, patients switched to every-other-week dosing retained 83%-97% of their initial weight loss over the next 12 weeks. Monthly cohorts retained 82%-90%, versus 61% for patients switched to placebo. However, a label for less-frequent dosing may come later, supported by the larger Vanquish extension studies. “But it seems more likely that the VANQUISH extension data would be sort of a standalone package that would be a supplement later. But again, too early to say definitively,” Lian said. A second maintenance study, including a switch from injections to daily tablets, is expected to report results in 2027. Viking also plans to start a 28-day multiple-dose study of its amylin drug VK3019 in the first quarter of 2027. Shares of Iovance Biotherapeutics (IOVA) jumped 12% in extended trading on Wednesday as an upcoming lung-cancer data presentation fueled optimism about its cell therapy’s potential beyond melanoma. IOVA stock rose nearly 2% Wednesday, bringing its weekly gain to 5% and putting it on track for a second straight week of gains. The company said it will share positive results for Lifileucel in previously treated advanced lung cancer on Thursday. The announcement comes after encouraging results in sarcoma and melanoma, adding to interest in how widely the treatment could be used. The trial tests one-time Lifileucel tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy in previously treated nonsquamous metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC). The company will also discuss precision-medicine opportunities for its TIL platform in lung cancer. At ESMO, it presented research examining tumor-reactive T-cell clones in patients who responded to Lifileucel. Lifileucel is already sold as Amtagvi for previously treated advanced melanoma. The lung-cancer announcement came just two days after Iovance reported early results in two soft tissue cancers: undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) and dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS). Four of the first eight evaluable patients had confirmed partial responses, giving the small pilot trial a 50% objective response rate. All four responses were ongoing at the Sept. 9 cutoff, lasting at least six weeks and at least 46 weeks. Patients had received between one and seven prior systemic treatments. Iovance said the safety findings were consistent with the Lifileucel treatment regimen in other cancers. “This level of durability provides meaningful time for patients with refractory UPS and DDLPS suffering from high disease burden, poor quality of life, and a lack of effective treatments, including no approved immunotherapy options,” said Lauren Banks, the trial’s principal investigator and a sarcoma medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. Iovance is now enrolling patients in its Phase 2 Saratoga registrational trial in the two sarcoma types. Lifileucel received FDA fast track designation for advanced UPS and DDLPS in the second quarter of 2026. The company’s recent updates also included final Phase 2 results, released last week, for Lifileucel combined with Pembrolizumab in previously untreated advanced melanoma. Of the 24 patients studied, 62.5% had a confirmed response, including 29.2% who achieved a complete response. Median overall survival had not been reached after a median study follow-up of 50.9 months. “About half of patients do not experience lasting benefit with frontline combination immunotherapy for advanced melanoma,” said trial investigator Andrew J.S. Furness. The results support Iovance’s ongoing Phase 3 Tilvance-301 study, which compares Lifileucel plus Pembrolizumab with Pembrolizumab alone. The trial will support approval for earlier use in advanced melanoma and serve as the confirmatory study for full U.S. approval of Amtagvi in previously treated advanced melanoma. title: Microsoft Stock Has One Thing Left To Prove - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. Microsoft (MSFT) says customer demand for cloud capacity exceeds its available supply, and some third-party capacity expected in the September quarter was delayed. Management now expects a portion of that capacity to arrive in the second half of its fiscal year, leaving the shortage unresolved. You need to know first which part of Microsoft is short, and how much revenue comes from it. Even with the delayed third-party deliveries, management said Azure revenue grew 48% in fiscal Q1 2027, the quarter that ended September 30, 2026. Management cited Foundry, Microsoft’s platform for building AI solutions, alongside earning more on its processors as drivers of that growth. During the October 28, 2026 call, analysts asked how Microsoft would earn a return as it adds AI capacity, and what was behind the AI demand in Azure. Addressing returns, Microsoft’s Satya Nadella pointed to both running Azure more efficiently and earning more from each workload. He said Microsoft wants a single pool of capacity that is as efficient and interchangeable as possible. Azure is part of the Microsoft Cloud, which generated $63.9 billion of the company’s $92.3 billion in revenue that quarter. That accounts for more than two-thirds of Microsoft’s sales. Growth for Microsoft Cloud accelerated to 30%, compared with 19% for the company as a whole. Azure brings in only a portion of that total, which also includes M365 Commercial Cloud. Management has said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, and that some supply it had counted on for the December quarter has also moved into the second half of the fiscal year. Even so, the company expects Azure revenue to grow 49% to 50% in the December quarter, excluding currency swings, with efficiency gains across its fleet of chips helping to offset some delayed GPU contracts. Microsoft is paying heavily for the build-out. Management expects capital spending of about $170 billion for calendar 2026, a total it said reflects the third-party delays. It expects spending to speed up in the second half of its fiscal year, including the third-party deliveries that shifted there. Free cash flow was $18.6 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, down from $25.7 billion a year earlier, a drop management put down to higher capital spending. It still expects free cash flow to stay positive in fiscal 2027. The Azure guide covers only the December quarter. Management also said token pricing, which is what customers pay per unit of AI output, could change during the quarter. When Will Microsoft Report Azure’s Next Growth Rate? Microsoft is expected to report its fiscal Q2 2027 results, covering the December quarter, in January 2027. The number to watch in that report is Azure’s growth rate, set beside management’s guide for the quarter on the same basis, excluding currency swings. If you own an S&P 500 or Nasdaq fund, you already own Microsoft, alongside the same few giants that lead those funds. title: I Graded Microsoft's Latest Report on 3 Things. Here's My Verdict on the Stock. - The Motley Fool
content: Azure grew faster than management's own forecast. Is that enough to make the stock a buy around $530? Microsoft (MSFT -1.55%) posted results for the fiscal first quarter of 2027 (the three months ending Sept. 30, 2026) on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Revenue climbed 19% year over year to $92.3 billion, and earnings per share grew 18% on a non-GAAP (adjusted) basis. The stock hardly moved. Shares trade near $530 as I write, about 2% under the record close of $543.45 they set on Oct. 13. This quiet response makes sense to me. The quarter combined great growth in Microsoft's cloud business with another big jump in spending. I graded the report on the three things I think matter most to shareholders today: Azure's growth against the company's own forecast, spending and margins, and the outlook. In early September, Microsoft narrowed what it counts as revenue from Azure, its cloud computing platform, and changed its forecast to match. The forecast was for Azure revenue growth of 44% to 45% in constant currency in the fiscal first quarter. Azure instead grew 48%. And it did that even though some third-party data center capacity Microsoft expected in the quarter was late. Showing how high demand for the platform still is, Azure's growth has sped up sharply over the last year. Under the new definition, it grew 40% a year ago, 42% in the fiscal fourth quarter (the period that ended in June), then 48% in the September quarter. In other words, Azure is growing faster today than it was a year ago, even after passing $100 billion in revenue in fiscal 2026. Somebody is going to make a fortune on Anthropic’s IPO. It probably won’t be regular investors waiting for the day it goes public. Unless investors know where to look. Because two companies anyone can buy today already own pieces of Anthropic. And one of them owns a piece of OpenAI, too. "Customer demand continues to exceed available supply," CFO Amy Hood said on the company's fiscal first-quarter earnings call. Earlier this month, I wrote that I thought Microsoft shares needed Azure to keep growing faster than 40%. It cleared that bar easily. Capital expenditures came to $45.2 billion in the fiscal first quarter. This compares to $34.9 billion a year ago (up around 30%) and $41 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter. Of course, the total could have been higher had the delayed capacity arrived on time. The spending is hurting free cash flow. Cash flow from operations climbed 29% year over year to $58 billion. But free cash flow dropped around 27% to $18.6 billion, down from $25.7 billion a year earlier and $19.6 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter. Yes, Microsoft's operating margin inched up to 50%, from 49% a year ago. But Microsoft Cloud's gross margin dipped to 66%, from 68% a year earlier, because lower-margin Azure made up a bigger part of cloud sales. The money is going into capacity that customers already want. Still, free cash flow shrinking while profits grow isn't a trend I can grade far higher. For the fiscal second quarter, management forecast revenue between $96 billion and $97.1 billion, or growth of 18% to 19%, around the same rate as the fiscal first quarter. More importantly, management expects Azure revenue to climb 49% to 50% in constant currency. But management also expects operating margins to dip slightly year over year. And it sees Windows OEM and devices revenue dropping in the mid-30% range, partly because of lower PC demand and a year-ago quarter that got a boost from the end of Windows 10 support. Plus, capital expenditures should pass $50 billion in the fiscal second quarter, taking spending in calendar 2026 to around $170 billion. I'd still call it a strong outlook, as Azure is arguably the figure that matters most for the stock. Overall, the report gets an A, a C+, and a B+, which is better than I thought going in. In the past four reported quarters, Microsoft's adjusted earnings per share totaled about $18.04. With the stock around $530, shares cost about 29 times adjusted earnings. Before the report, the stock cost about 31 times adjusted earnings. Last weekend, I wrote that I'd want to buy the stock closer to $465. The Azure grade is what moves me. With growth well above my 40% bar, I'm less worried the stock might deserve a lower price-to-earnings multiple than I used. And because my buy price is linked to adjusted earnings, a quarter like this raises it. But the spending grade stops me from paying $530. With free cash flow shrinking, I think 29 times adjusted earnings already reflects most of the good news. I'm closer to buying than I was a week ago. But I'd still want a lower price. Microsoft (NasdaqGS:MSFT) completed a record US$25b multi-tranche bond sale, its first major issuance in nearly a decade. The company said proceeds will support long term funding for AI infrastructure and continued investment in its cloud platforms. Microsoft also expanded its AI collaboration with The Estée Lauder Companies to apply data and decision intelligence across global beauty brands. Microsoft's US$25b bond raise and new Estée Lauder AI partnership deserve a close look alongside the rest of our assessment. Check out 2 warning signs (1 major) that Microsoft investors should know about. For a wider read on where money is flowing into AI buildout, it is worth comparing Microsoft with peers exposed to 54 AI infrastructure stocks. Microsoft runs a global software and cloud platform that underpins everything from workplace productivity to large scale enterprise computing. Fresh capital and new AI partnerships reflect how the company aims to shape the next wave of business and consumer technology usage. Using a large multi tranche bond sale lets Microsoft lock in long term funding for AI data centers and cloud hardware without drawing down as much on current cash. Debt financing also spreads the cost of its US$170b to US$190b calendar 2026 capex plans over time, which can preserve flexibility for dividends, buybacks, or acquisitions. The new fixed and floating rate notes add senior, unsecured liabilities across maturities from 2 to 40 years, which increases total debt but staggers repayment obligations. With a AAA rating and strong earnings, interest costs are supported, although investors still need to watch leverage metrics such as net debt to free cash flow as AI spending continues. One checkpoint is how free cash flow and Microsoft Cloud margins trend over the next four quarters as the US$25b funding is deployed. If Azure and AI related revenue supports operating margin near current levels while net debt to free cash flow remains contained, this would indicate that AI capex is being absorbed without putting undue pressure on the balance sheet. Meanwhile, Nasdaq-100 futures lost 1.2%. S&P 500 futures declined 0.5%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures lost 17 points, or 0.03% at the time of writing. Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF jumped about 2% each on Wednesday as gains in AMD, Micron Tech (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO). The broader Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) rose 0.6%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for SPY improved to ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’, while it remained in ‘bearish’ territory for DIA and QQQ. The Federal Reserve opted to keep its target interest rate steady on Wednesday, but financial markets focused on Chair Kevin Warsh's announcement of a structural shift in the frequency of future interest rate decisions. The central bank held interest rates steady at 3.75% to 4% amid elevated inflation and a strong job market. The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10–2 vote. Under Warsh’s revamped framework, the FOMC will issue rate decisions at seven of its eight scheduled sessions in 2027, reserving one meeting exclusively for broad monetary policy strategy without issuing a formal rate statement. By 2028, the central bank plans to reduce its rate-setting votes to six per year, leaving two gatherings devoted entirely to strategic evaluations. “The Fed appears comfortable being patient for now as financial conditions have evolved broadly in line with expectations,” Luis Alvarado at Wells Fargo Investment Institute told Bloomberg. “But patience should not be confused with complacency.” Meanwhile, Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) shares slid about 11% after-hours after it reported third-quarter financial results that highlighted strong top-line revenue growth across its core digital ad and cloud operations, though massive investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure and investment losses squeezed profitability. Shares of Lumentum Holdings Inc (LITE) soared 10% after hours on Wednesday following a report that Marvell Technology is in talks to buy it in a potential megadeal. A deal between Marvell and the data center optics maker could be announced as soon as next week, Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter. A final deal hasn’t been reached, and details could change, the report said. After Wednesday’s market close, Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, while Marvell is valued near $221 billion. Shares of MRVL tumbled 8% following the report. Marvell is a fabless semiconductor designer focused on data-infrastructure solutions, while Lumentum makes optical and photonic products such as lasers, optical components, and networking systems used in cloud and AI data centers. Lumentum’s indium-phosphide technology is particularly in high demand; CEO Michael Hurlston has previously said that the company is essentially sold out of certain products into 2029 and is under-shipping demand by substantial margins due to the fast-paced nature of AI data center buildouts. Marvell, too, is strengthening its position in  the AI space, recently inking a partnership with Google on custom chips. The company also completed acquiring Celestial AI, specialized in photonic interconnect technology to remove data bottlenecks in AI data centers, earlier this year. A potential combination would give Marvell access to scarce, high-performance optical components which can help ease bottlenecks in AI clusters by replacing copper interconnects which are more limited in capacity. (MSFT) share price inched 3% higher after-hours on Wednesday after the software maker’s first-quarter results surpassed Wall Street expectations, propelled by surging demand for its artificial intelligence tools and cloud computing platform. For the three months ended Sept. 30, the technology giant reported total revenue of $92.3 billion, representing a 19% increase compared to the same period last year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share reached $4.89, outpacing average analyst projections of $4.72. "We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack," said Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft. "By helping organizations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry." The core driver of the quarter’s growth was the company's cloud operations. Total Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $63.9 billion, an increase of 30% year-over-year. Sales at Azure, Microsoft’s flagship cloud computing division, jumped 48%, surpassing Wall Street estimates of 44% growth. Commercial remaining performance obligation—a key measure of future contracted revenue—soared 73% to $677 billion, signaling sustained enterprise commitment to Microsoft's ecosystem. In the Agents and Infrastructure segment, total revenue rose 25% to $76.8 billion. Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue saw an 18% increase on an adjusted basis, while consumer cloud sales grew 17%. "We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year," said Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer. "Results exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and earnings per share." To keep pace with computing demands for AI workloads, Microsoft expanded its capital expenditures by 30% to $45.2 billion for the quarter. The heavy spending comes as major tech companies face increased investor scrutiny over data center outlays, though analysts noted Microsoft's execution remains disciplined relative to market expectations. However, even amid rising capex, the firm’s free cash flow remained net positive, helping calm some markets that the AI buildout spend might not generate required revenue and in turn weigh on financials. Meanwhile, performance in consumer-facing divisions was mixed. The Devices and Consumer segment recorded $15.5 billion in revenue, down 3% from the prior-year period. While search and advertising revenue (excluding traffic acquisition costs) gained 12%, Windows OEM and devices revenue dropped 22%, and Xbox content and services revenue slipped 2%. Microsoft expects Q2 revenue to come in between $96 and $97.1 billion, higher than the $95.6 billion analysts polled by Fiscal.ai expect. The company also expects its capex to soar to $50 billion in Q2, while expecting its cash flow to remain net positive for the whole of FY27. Shares of Nvidia Corp (NVDA) slipped 1% on Wednesday  following reports that the U.S. Department of Justice has inquired about how its planned acquisition of Hugging Face could affect competition in artificial intelligence. According to a report from Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, department officials have asked whether the Hugging Face deal would allow Nvidia to control a key distribution point for AI models and tools. The questioning adds to the years-long probe by antitrust regulators on Nvidia’s conduct, which kicked off under former President Joe Biden, the report said. The probe is reportedly continuing with no indication that current President Donald Trump has any involvement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has a relationship with Trump and recently joined the President on his diplomatic trip to China. The DOJ’s recent line of questioning covers the company’s acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and whether it has pressured customers, sources told Reuters. As part of the probe, the DOJ has reportedly examined Nvidia’s other acquisition deals, including the December 2025 deal to buy SchedMD, sources told Reuters. The department has also scrutinized Nvidia's conduct following other transactions, including its licensing deal with chip startup Groq and its acquisition of Run.ai, the report added. Nvidia announced in early September that it had agreed to buy Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion. The transaction includes roughly $11.9 billion payable to Hugging Face’s investors and an equity-based retention program of up to about $1 billion for employees who join Nvidia. Hugging Face operates a widely used platform that hosts millions of open-source AI models, datasets, and applications, serving millions of developers and hundreds of thousands of companies. It is often described as a central hub for open AI development. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pledged that the platform will remain open to models, frameworks, clouds, and computing platforms from across the industry, and that Nvidia’s own chips will not be required to use it. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027. The forecast heavily outperformed Wall Street expectations, as data compiled by Bloomberg and FactSet indicated that analysts anticipated the metric to remain deeply negative during that period. Fueling the optimism is a robust revenue trajectory. Oracle reaffirmed its target of $225 billion in total revenue by fiscal 2030, signaling an average annual growth rate of roughly 35%. Operating margins are projected to climb past 40% by the end of the decade. To manage the heavy capital expenditures required for the build-out, Oracle outlined a disciplined funding strategy, which included a pledge to limit total additional funding needs between fiscal 2027 and 2030 to $20 billion, split evenly between equity and debt. The company is executing a massive data center build-out to support major clients like OpenAI, stepping into direct competition with established hyperscalers like Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOGL). Maxson noted that Oracle plans to deliver an additional seven gigawatts of data center capacity over the next couple of years, pushing its total fleet capacity beyond 10 gigawatts by the conclusion of fiscal 2028. To put the scale in perspective, a single gigawatt of electricity generates enough power for about 750,000 U.S. homes at once. While Oracle hit negative $23.7 billion cash flow in the fiscal year ending May 2026 due to infrastructure costs, executives emphasized that capital expenditures will peak through the current and upcoming fiscal years before declining significantly in fiscal 2029. Shares of Hims & Hers (HIMS) jumped 5% on Wednesday after the Department of Health and Human Services said it would temporarily allow compounding pharmacies to produce six popular peptides. HHS said it will not go after state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities, or licensed doctors for compounding six peptides—BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, and TB-500—as long as they follow basic rules on ingredient quality, manufacturing, safety reporting, labeling, and prescriptions written for individual patients. “...based on the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) meeting and data regarding utilization of peptides, HHS believes that there is significant interest in the use of these peptides in compounding,” HHS said, referring to the advisory committee recommendation in July that some peptides be considered for compounding. The new policy is temporary while the FDA completes formal rulemaking on the official list of bulk substances that can be used in compounding. Compounders must report serious adverse events with the use of the drugs or any product quality issues such as contamination to the FDA, HHS added.  Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Hims has already prepared for a potential approval of peptide compounding by securing a California peptide facility and testing ingredients, while signaling interest in offering items such as sermorelin, glutathione, and NAD+ depending on final regulatory outcomes. Peptides used for recovery, inflammation, sleep, and related wellness goals have drawn strong consumer interest online, even without formal FDA approval. “We have spent years building the infrastructure we need in our very own US-based peptide manufacturing facility, developing dosing protocols with clinical experts, and setting up frameworks to better understand these emerging treatments,” the company’s Chief Medical Officer Anant Vinjamoori said after the HHS directive in a post on X. HIMS CEO Andrew Dudum also termed it “encouraging progress.” HIMS, however, has also faced setbacks this year, including an FTC lawsuit filed in late July alleging deceptive privacy practices involving data sharing with advertising platforms and misleading billing or cancellation practices. The company transitioned from offering compounded GLP-1s to branded versions earlier this year, pressuring margins despite subscriber growth. content: The Estée Lauder Companies (EL) announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft (MSFT) on Friday to strengthen its cloud and data infrastructure and support the responsible adoption of AI across its business. “Our partnership with Microsoft, in addition to the other strategic partners in our One Operating Ecosystem, is powering our teams with the capabilities to ultimately deliver more relevant, personalized experiences that meet consumers’ evolving needs,” said Brian Franz, chief technology and transformation officer at Estée Lauder. The company said the platform is designed to reduce duplication, enable reusable data products and improve access to data-driven insights. The company is also investing in a Unified Consumer Data Platform to deepen its understanding of consumer needs and preferences. Combined with connected product data, the platform is designed to support personalized experiences from product discovery to purchase and inform product innovation, drawing on the company’s 80 years of consumer understanding and beauty expertise. Separately, Estée Lauder is developing a connected, AI-powered workflow across product design, validation and manufacturing. The initiative aims to help teams make faster, more coordinated decisions and move products from idea to launch more efficiently. Franz said the partnership’s enhanced capabilities would help Estée Lauder “drive sustainable growth, improve productivity, and support margin expansion,” while creating capacity for reinvestment. Microsoft Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer Deb Cupp said the collaboration would help turn insights into action at scale, from empowering employees to modernizing product development and delivering more meaningful consumer experiences. title: Should You Buy And Hold Microsoft Stock? - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. Microsoft (MSFT) stock has returned 30.5% since April 30, 2026, against 7.7% for the S&P 500. A buyer today is paying for a run that has already happened. Yet the shares trade at 27.6 times earnings, which falls below the 31.5 average of the stock’s readings at its last 12 fiscal quarter ends. If you bought at today’s price and held for three years, what could the shares return? One Scenario Puts Microsoft’s Three-Year Return Near 48% Under one set of assumptions, holding Microsoft for three years would return about 48.1%, before dividends. This scenario assumes revenue grows 15.2% a year, representing 85% of Microsoft’s latest twelve-month pace, and the P/E stays at today’s level. The year-three net margin incorporates a blend: 70% of today’s margin and 30% of its average at earlier fiscal quarter ends. Here is how today’s figures compare with year three of the scenario. Higher sales account for 108.3% of the gain. This is more than all of it because 8.3% is lost to the slightly lower margin, and none of the gain comes from the P/E. The cloud business has grown the fastest recently. Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 29.7% in fiscal 2026, against 15.9% for Productivity and Business Processes. More Personal Computing revenue fell 1.1% that year. When an older business shrinks, newer ones have to carry the company’s growth. Tesla shows the risk when nothing newer does: it got 98% of last quarter’s deliveries from the Model 3 and Model Y after shelving its cheaper car. Read Trefis Big Story: How Tesla Blundered. To achieve this gain, Microsoft has to keep turning cloud demand into revenue. In fiscal Q1 2027, Azure revenue grew 48% from a year earlier, a result management credited to Foundry and improved CPU monetization. On the October 28, 2026 call, management said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, and Microsoft added 24 new data centers in the quarter. Management’s guide for fiscal Q2 2027 forecasts revenue growth of 18% to 19%. This estimate covers one quarter rather than three years. It is in line with the 18.8% Microsoft reported for fiscal Q1 2027. Microsoft is spending heavily on the new data centers, and on October 29 it priced $25 billion of new debt to help fund the build-out. Capital spending was $45.2 billion in fiscal Q1 2027. Free cash flow fell to $18.6 billion from $25.7 billion a year earlier, even as cash from operations rose. How Microsoft’s Return Changes If An Assumption Shifts Changing one assumption at a time while keeping the other two identical to the scenario yields the following three-year returns. Of the changes in the table, only holding the stock for five years instead of three lifts the return above the scenario’s. The margin starts from an unusual high. Microsoft’s twelve-month net margin is the highest recorded at any fiscal quarter end from fiscal Q2 2017 on, against an average of 36.8% at the 12 quarter ends before the latest. The latest quarter alone came in at 39.7%. One quarter inside those twelve months, fiscal Q2 2026, posted a 47.3% net margin, coming in above its 47.1% operating margin. Microsoft said a gain tied to OpenAI’s recapitalization drove other income to $10 billion in that quarter. With the earlier average below today’s level, the year-three margin in the scenario comes out lower. Taken one at a time, revenue growth could slow from the 17.9% Microsoft delivered over the twelve months to fiscal Q1 2027 down to 1.1% a year before three years of holding returned nothing. The net margin could fall from 41.2% to 26.9% before the same happened. The P/E could fall to 18.6, slipping below its lowest reading of 20.7 at any fiscal quarter end since fiscal Q2 2017. Under these assumptions, the return comes from Microsoft selling more, led by its cloud business, and not from a higher P/E. Microsoft’s revenue growth is the measure to watch in its fiscal Q2 2027 report, expected in January 2027. Not necessarily on Microsoft alone, if your goal is long-term wealth. Microsoft announced on Thursday that it plans to issue $25 billion in bonds, leveraging its strong credit rating to raise funds for infrastructure expansion. Zhitong Finance APP learned that Microsoft (MSFT.US) announced on Thursday its plan to issue $25 billion in bonds, leveraging its strong credit rating to raise funds for infrastructure expansion. The software giant holds the highest AAA credit rating from S&P. The company's management plans to increase capital expenditures to $170 billion by 2026, in order to meet the robust demand for computing power from AI labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients. According to a statement, Microsoft will issue senior unsecured notes with a total principal amount of $25 billion, divided into floating-rate and fixed-rate tranches. "Microsoft intends to use the net proceeds from this offering for general corporate purposes, which may include funding working capital, capital expenditures, share repurchases, acquisitions, and the repayment of existing debt," the company said. The offering is expected to close on November 4. According to reports, Amazon (AMZN.US) and Alphabet (GOOGL.US) have entered the bond market this year to finance infrastructure projects, while CoreWeave (CRWV.US), which focuses on AI cloud services, has also leveraged the debt market to expand its data center footprint. Microsoft's last issuance of high-rated bonds dates back to 2017, when it raised $17 billion. However, as major central banks raise interest rates to combat inflation, investors' risk appetite for highly indebted companies continues to decline. Microsoft Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood stated during the company's earnings call on Wednesday that, when conditions are attractive, Microsoft will secure additional sources of financing to supplement its own cash flow generation. "Leasing is also a financing tool we are currently utilizing," she said. "Leveraging our rating advantages, we have access to funding in the bond market, though we have not yet tapped into this capacity." On Wednesday, Microsoft reported positive free cash flow, in stark contrast to Alphabet, whose cash flow has been negative for the second consecutive quarter.
